related_questions.question: What are the three types of damages available in a civil case?

text_blocks.snippet: In civil cases, the three main types of damages are compensatory, punitive, and nominal. Compensatory damages aim to reimburse the plaintiff for losses caused by the defendant's actions. Punitive damages are meant to punish the defendant for egregious conduct. Nominal damages are awarded when a legal right has been violated, but the actual loss is minimal or unquantifiable.

list.title: Compensatory Damages:
list.snippet: These are the most common type of damages and are designed to compensate the plaintiff for their losses. They can be further divided into:
Economic Damages: These are quantifiable monetary losses, such as medical bills, lost wages, property damage, and other out-of-pocket expenses.
Non-economic Damages: These are subjective, non-monetary losses, such as pain and suffering, emotional distress, loss of enjoyment of life, and loss of companionship.

list.title: Punitive Damages:
list.snippet: These are awarded to punish the defendant for intentional, malicious, or grossly negligent conduct, and to deter similar behavior in the future.

list.title: Nominal Damages:
list.snippet: These are awarded when a legal right has been violated, but the plaintiff has not suffered any actual monetary loss. Typically, a small, symbolic sum is awarded.
